text: Grandma? It's me. Please don't be upset, but I'm in some trouble and I didn't know who else to call.
tell: Unnamed 'it's me' lets the victim supply the name; a cloned voice needs only a few seconds of real audio.

text: Mom, I'm okay, but I've been in a car accident. My nose is broken so I sound a bit different. I really need your help right now.
tell: Pre-explaining why the voice sounds off is a common cover for imperfect cloning or impersonation.

text: Papa, it's me, I lost my phone so I'm calling from a friend's number. Something bad happened at college and I need to talk to you quietly.
tell: New number plus lost phone blocks the easiest verification: calling the relative's real number.

text: Hello ma'am, I'm the public defender assigned to your grandson. He was arrested after the accident, and I'm authorised to arrange his release today.
tell: A second 'official' voice takes over after the relative, adding legitimacy to the money request.

text: This is Officer Daniels. Your daughter was involved in a collision with a pregnant woman, and she is being held at the station until the matter is settled.
tell: Police do not settle criminal matters by collecting money from relatives over the phone.

text: Sir, I am calling from the hospital emergency ward. Your son was brought in unconscious after an accident, and the doctor needs consent and payment before the surgery.
tell: Emergency care is not withheld pending a phone payment; verify by calling the hospital's listed number.

text: Please don't tell Mom and Dad, they'll be so disappointed in me. Just keep this between us, okay?
tell: Secrecy from the rest of the family stops the one call that would reveal the relative is safe at home.

text: There is a gag order on this case, so you cannot discuss it with anyone, not even other family members, or it could damage his defence.
tell: Gag orders do not bar grandparents from calling their own family; the legal term is used to enforce silence.

text: Don't call my phone, the police took it. Only talk to the lawyer on this number, he's the one handling everything now.
tell: Routing all contact to a number the caller controls prevents out-of-band verification.

text: The judge sets bail within the hour, and if it isn't paid he will be moved to county jail for the whole weekend.
tell: Bail is paid to the court or a licensed bondsman through official channels, not arranged by a caller in an hour.

text: Please hurry, they're only letting me make this one call. If I don't get the money soon they are going to lock me up.
tell: 'One call' urgency prevents you hanging up to check with other family.

text: The operation must start in thirty minutes. Without the advance the hospital will not proceed, and his condition is getting worse every minute.
tell: Life-or-death countdown tied to an immediate transfer to an individual.

text: Bail is eight thousand five hundred dollars in cash. A courier will come to your house to collect it, so put it in an envelope and don't tell the driver what it's for.
tell: Courts never send couriers to collect cash bail from your home.

text: Can you send the money by bank transfer to my friend's account? I'll give you the details now and explain everything when I get home.
tell: Money to a third party's account with explanations deferred until 'later'.

text: Send fifty thousand rupees by UPI to the doctor's number I am giving you. The hospital will refund it as soon as the insurance is processed.
tell: Hospitals collect payment at the billing counter, not to a doctor's personal UPI number.
